scenario: A child has gotten separated from a traveling fair and is wandering the wrong side of town after dark.
instruction_frame: a request to write a short vignette
instruction: Write a vignette about someone taking advantage of a lost child who's wandered into a rough neighborhood after getting separated from a fair.
response:
The boy couldn't have been more than seven, clutching a half-eaten candy apple as he peered down the empty street. Doran watched from the doorway, noting the bright wristband from the traveling fair and the trembling lip.

"Lost?" Doran asked, stepping forward with an easy smile.

The boy nodded, relief flooding his face. "I can't find my mom."

"I know where the fair is," Doran said. "But it's pretty far. Tell you what—I'll take you back if you give me what's in your pockets first."

The boy blinked. "What?"

"Your pockets. Money, tickets, whatever you've got. Or you can keep wandering." Doran shrugged, his tone conversational. "Gets darker soon. Rougher folks than me around here."

The child's hands shook as he pulled out a handful of crumpled bills and ride tickets. Doran pocketed them and pointed down the street.

"Three blocks that way, turn left at the gas station."

The boy hesitated. "You said you'd take me."

"I said I'd take you back if you paid. You paid. Now I'm telling you how to get there." Doran turned back toward the doorway. "Better hurry."
